headline: Military contracts swell. Space diplomacy expands. Cash flows.
deck: This week highlights robust military spending and a flurry of international agreements.

stories.head: Viasat secures hefty Marine Corps contract
stories.body: Viasat has won a $307 million contract to provide satellite communications for the Marine Corps, underscoring that military budgets still have room for a few more zeros. This contract is part of the ongoing trend of defense spending that prioritizes connectivity in modern warfare. With military budgets tightening elsewhere, this win might just be a sign of shifting priorities.
stories.soWhat: If Viasat can keep landing these contracts, it might just become the poster child for military spending resilience.

stories.head: Rocket Lab’s growth strategy includes acquisitions
stories.body: Rocket Lab announced its largest launch contract to date and plans to acquire a space robotics company, suggesting that sometimes you have to buy your friends to grow. The contract is part of a broader strategy to solidify its position in the launch market, which is becoming increasingly competitive. The acquisition could provide Rocket Lab with the necessary tech boost to enhance its service offerings.
stories.soWhat: If Rocket Lab can integrate the robotics expertise effectively, it might just leapfrog competitors still focusing on pure launch services.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid defense focus
stories.body: True Anomaly has successfully raised $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, which are increasingly critical for defense applications. This round highlights the growing investor interest in companies that can address national security challenges in space.
stories.soWhat: With defense budgets expanding, True Anomaly’s focus could position it as a key player in the next wave of military tech.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Rocket Lab’s acquisition
watchlist.body: The integration of a robotics company could redefine Rocket Lab's service capabilities and competitive landscape.

watchlist.title: Palantir’s TITAN extension implications
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension could signal increasing demand for ground station capabilities in defense.

watchlist.title: Paraguay's Artemis Accords signing effects
watchlist.body: As the sixth country to sign, Paraguay’s involvement may spur more nations to join the Accords.

watchlist.title: Watch for hypersonic testing delays
watchlist.body: The ongoing delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests could impact future defense projects and funding.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
